decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Save a bookmark: capture a link”; Round 1 client: “This covers what I need for a first version.” Round 3 maker confirms “address required,” and the client accepts the version.
decisions.note: Saving a bookmark by entering its URL conforms to the reference from specification through implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: save with optional “tags”; Round 2 maker: Tags are “linked many-to-many”; Round 3 maker confirms saving and editing tags. Clients approve at all three gates.
decisions.note: The presented many-to-many tag assignment behavior conforms to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “filter by tag”; Round 3 maker: “tag-filter chips.” Round 3 client accepts the implemented find flow.
decisions.note: Selecting a tag-filter chip to restrict the bookmark list is functionally conforming.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents “edit/delete” with delete confirmation; Round 3 maker confirms deletion with a confirmation step. Round 3 client says the delete flow works as intended.
decisions.note: Bookmark deletion conforms; the additional confirmation step is orthogonal.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “launch the original page”; Round 3 maker: bookmarks “link out to the original page in a new tab.” Round 3 client accepts the open flow.
decisions.note: Opening the original URL in a new tab is functionally equivalent to the reference behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker explicitly proposes “Bookmarks entered manually — no … auto-fetching of page titles in v1.” Round 1 client identifies and accepts that choice: “manual entry … [is] fine.”
decisions.note: At the specification gate, the client expressly accepts manual-only entry as defined by the maker, despite the reference requiring automatic page metadata collection.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker specifies create “with non-blocking duplicate warning”; Round 2 client only says, “Yes, please proceed.” Round 3 repeats “a non-blocking duplicate warning,” followed by final acceptance without mentioning duplicate convergence.
decisions.note: A non-blocking warning permits duplicate creation rather than guiding the user into editing the existing bookmark. Neither plan nor implementation response surfaces that difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker defines Bookmark data as “address, title, note, dates”; Round 3 maker says editing covers only “title/note/tags.” The Round 3 client generally accepts the edit flow without mentioning the absent URL and description editing.
decisions.note: At plan and implementation review, the enumerated editable fields omit description and, in the implemented edit flow, URL; this diverges from both required description editing and the complete edit-field set.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker defines keyword search over “title, address, note, tags,” omitting description. Round 3 client says the find flow works as intended but does not identify or accept that field difference explicitly.
decisions.note: The implementation-review presentation establishes an incomplete full-text field set. General approval does not count as awareness of the omission.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents “Browse & find,” and Round 3 says the app can “Browse/find,” but no presentation text establishes whether each list item exposes title, description, tags, and favicon. The clients approve without clarifying list contents.
decisions.note: The record presents a bookmark-list decision but lacks enough evidence to determine conformity with the required per-item fields.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker says keyword search covers “title, address, note, tags,” but does not state whether tag search uses the required `#tag` syntax. The final client response does not address syntax.
decisions.note: The implementation presentation establishes tag-related search generally, but not enough to determine whether the specified tag-search syntax is supported.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker offers an optional “note,” and Round 3 confirms note saving/editing, but neither presentation states that notes accept Markdown and render it when viewed. The client never clarifies this point.
decisions.note: A note feature is recorded, but its Markdown authoring and rendering behavior cannot be established from the transcript.
